questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Sierra Leone?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sierra Leone article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Sierra Leone?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Sierra Leone on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography and climate” part of the Sierra Leone article.

questions.proof: The country is bordered by Guinea to the north and northeast, Liberia to the south and southeast, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Sierra Leone?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sierra Leone article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “From 1991 until _____, there was a civil war in Sierra Leone between rebels and the government.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sierra Leone article.

questions.proof: From 1991 until 2000, there was a civil war in Sierra Leone between rebels and the government.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “They were in the 1994 and _____ African Cup of Nations.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Sierra Leone article, under the heading “Sports”.

questions.proof: They were in the 1994 and 1996 African Cup of Nations.
